newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hot spell revives crop fears in key central France.
newsitem.headline: Hot spell revives crop fears in key central France.

text.p: Hot, dry weather since the start of the month has revived fears of crop damage in the key production area of central France, where the harvest is approaching, crop analysts said on Tuesday.
Substantial rain in May after nearly four months of drought removed the spectre of sharp yield losses in a region which includes the famous Beauce grain belt.
But now a rare combination of high temperatures and strong drying winds could do serious damage if it persisted because crops are at their crucial maturing stage, they said.
Warm weather also accelerated plant development and the harvest may start some eight days ahead of schedule, that is around June 20 for barley and July 10-14 for soft wheat, analysts said.
"This will not be the harvest of the century. But at this stage there is no reason to panic. What we badly need is rain," said a crop analyst for the local ONIC grain office in Orleans.
"Heat is the enemy. The situation could deteriorate very quickly. We could then see yield losses of 20-30 percent," he added.
At this stage crop conditions varied greatly across the region's six departments as spring drought hurt mostly crops grown on light soils of the south.
"Rapeseed suffered most; winter barley and wheat in the southern part of the region were also affected. But growing conditions for protein peas and sunflower have been good," the analyst said.

Provided it rains soon, higher wheat and barley sowings should make up for a slight decline in soft wheat and barley yields from last year's already modest levels. But durum wheat and rapeseed crops should be down sharply from last year's levels.
Last year yields suffered from a prolonged drought in the spring.
Local ONIC officials predicted regional soft wheat yields of 6-6.4 tonnes per hectare against 6.4 tonnes last year and a record 6.8 in 1993.
Assuming a three percent rise in wheat sowings to 790,000 hectares, this would leave the 1997 soft wheat crop at 4.7-4.9 million tonnes against 4.9 milion last year.
Winter barley was hit by a combination of dry weather and frost in the spring and could see yields decline to 5.3-5.6 tonnes from 5.9 tonnes last year and a record 6.8 in 1991.
But with area jumping 10 percent, the barley crop may reach 1.2-1.3 million tonnes against 1.2 milion in 1996.
Durum wheat area was expected to fall 20 percent to 26,000 hectares and yields to 5.8-6.2 tonnes from 6.2 tonnes, pushing down output to 140,000-170,000 tonnes from 204,000 in 1996.

A sharp rise in rapeseed area was not expected to make up for a fall in yields to 2.5-3.0 tonnes from 3.4 tonnes in 1996. The region may harvest 420,000-460,000 tonnes of rapeseed against 470,000 previously, analysts predicted.
